rv.q: This abundantly inventive production works best when it’s at its most surreally allusive – successfully and disconcertingly capturing the suppressed rage of 21st-century life.
The result is like slapping down a pile of newspapers, pointing at a phone, saying: “It’s bad, huh?” and taking a bow.
The Uncontainable Nausea of Alec Baldwin represents the very best of fringe theatre, delicately balancing a call for empathy with a darkly comic cautionary tale.

cn.t: This absurdist clown show about AI and violence divides critics sharply, with some praising its dizzying spectacle and timely themes while others find it a patience-testing trudge weakened by AI-generated scenes.
